Question Choices: Two figures are congruent if one can be mapped onto the other using what kind of transformations?
Question Answers: rigid transformations|rigid motions|a sequence of rigid transformations
Hints: These transformations preserve distance and angle measure.|Translations rotations and reflections qualify.
Solution: Translations, rotations and reflections are rigid motions: they preserve size and shape. Mapping one complete figure exactly onto the other by a rigid motion or a sequence of them establishes congruence.

Question Choices: Select. A dilation with scale factor 2 maps one triangle to another. Are the triangles necessarily congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Congruent triangles must have equal corresponding side lengths.|The dilation doubles all lengths.
Solution: No. The dilation multiplies every side length by 2. Corresponding positive side lengths therefore differ. Angles and side ratios are preserved, giving similarity, but not congruence.

Question Choices: Two angles are congruent exactly when they have the same what?
Hints: Congruence compares angle size.|Use degrees or radians to describe it.
Solution: Two angles are congruent exactly when their measures are equal. Their location, orientation and the drawn lengths of their rays do not affect this comparison.

Question Choices: Two segments are congruent exactly when they have the same what?
Hints: Congruence compares the distance between endpoints.|Direction and position do not matter.
Solution: Two segments are congruent exactly when their lengths, in the same units, are equal. Their direction and position do not matter.

Question Choices: Which triangle congruence criterion uses three pairs of corresponding sides?
Hints: No angle information is used.|The abbreviation repeats S three times.
Solution: SSS means side-side-side. Three pairs of equal corresponding side lengths determine the same triangle size and shape, up to rigid motion.

Question Choices: Which triangle congruence criterion uses two sides and their included angle?
Hints: The angle lies between the two known sides.|Read the data in order side angle side.
Solution: SAS means side-angle-side. Two pairs of corresponding sides and the angle included between those sides are equal, proving congruence.

Question Choices: Which triangle congruence criterion uses two angles and their included side?
Hints: The side lies between the two known angles.|Read the data in order angle side angle.
Solution: ASA means angle-side-angle. The two corresponding angle pairs match, and the equal side connects the vertices of those two angles.

Question Choices: Which triangle congruence criterion uses two angles and a nonincluded side?
Hints: The side is not between the known angles.|The abbreviation has the two A letters together.
Solution: AAS means angle-angle-side: two angles and a corresponding nonincluded side match. The third angles also match because each triangle totals 180 degrees, reducing the argument to ASA.

Question Choices: Why is SSA generally not a triangle congruence criterion?
Question Answers: it can produce two different triangles|two triangles are possible|ambiguous case|it is ambiguous
Hints: Imagine swinging the unknown vertex while keeping one side fixed.|The given data can fit more than one triangle.
Solution: SSA can allow two different positions for the remaining vertex, producing different third side lengths while preserving the given sides and nonincluded angle. Thus it can produce two noncongruent triangles and is not a general congruence criterion.

Question Choices: For right triangles which criterion uses a congruent hypotenuse and one congruent leg?
Hints: Both triangles must already be right triangles.|The abbreviation names the two known parts.
Solution: HL means hypotenuse-leg. Both triangles are right triangles and have equal hypotenuses and a corresponding equal leg. Pythagoras then fixes the other leg equally, so the triangles are congruent.
